doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Compliments from Johnny Mandel and Alec Wilder
summary: Johnny Mandel says Roy plays like he thinks; Wilder says Roy changes chords for the better and that Jackie's songs stay sung.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And my greatest compliment in the last couple of years came from Johnny Mandel. He came in to hear us at the Jazz Bakery in Los Angeles. We had a very good rhythm section that came with us from San Francisco. It was popping, everything was great. And we did one of his songs called “The Shining Sea,” which is a gorgeous melody. And I found — I explored ways to bring out more impressionistic sounds in it, just all kind of painting. And at the end he came out and we were talking and kicking stones and talking, and he said, “you know, you play like I think.” And that’s it. That’s my best compliment in my whole life.

The other one that I could relate is that Alec Wilder once said that we often break the rules but you don’t mind it. And he’s a stickler. He doesn’t like it when you take too many liberties, but he says, “well Roy changes my chords but usually they’re for the better.”
He said some very nice things about us too.

And one time he said a thing about me that I’ll never forget. He said “when she sings a song it stays sung.” He said that on his radio show when I did it with [sounds like] Loonis McLeun, the NPR show you know, and that thrilled me that he would say that, because you know he doesn’t mess around, he doesn’t say nice things if he doesn’t mean them.
